column1: # The argument list each documented introspection method is sent in
# class<TAB>method<TAB>arm<TAB>arguments, where `--` is a send with none.
# A LIST IS ONLY REAL IF THE ORACLE COMPLETES THE SEND. Any row the oracle
# refuses is a harness failure for that row and not a data point;
# introspection_arity.rs makes that a test failure. Without the rule the
# instrument reads green having sent nothing that could work.
# THE CLASS ARM IS HERE and corpus/collection-arguments.tsv's is not. This
# phase's own `loud` rows that live on it -- Package~defaultOptions,
# Routine~newFile -- are named by the plan's Tasks 4 and 7; an instance-only
# `UNSTABLE:` marks a row whose answered value the ORACLE does not reproduce
# between two of its own runs, so no value comparison could say anything
# about it. The value is not printed for such a row and the verdict is
# `unstable`; the marker is earned by running the oracle twice and is a test
# failure on a row whose two answers agree. Object~hashCode is address-derived
# and answers RAW BYTES rather than a printable number -- measured, three runs
# of one program put three different unprintable octet strings on stdout --
# so a probe of its own must not print one.
# `REFUSED:` marks a row the ORACLE refuses BY DESIGN, where the refusal is
# the measurement and no argument list would change it. The row is still
# compared on all three descriptors, and the rule is inverted rather than
# waived: a REFUSED row the oracle does complete is a test failure.
# Pointer's and Buffer's INSTANCE arm is deliberately absent -- no receiver
# exists for it. Their class arm is here.
# The receivers, the directives each needs and the two that are sent to from
